### 23.27.2 Ranking and stop rules

Choose work by expected benefit per engineering and trusted-code cost:
false-proof or omitted-obligation risk first; then common programs unblocked; then whole-workflow
wall time, CPU and memory saved; then maintenance and diagnostic clarity. Repair shared causes
before individual fixture exceptions. Instrument only enough to decide the next optimization.

A false accepted claim, missing obligation, stale product, trust downgrade, invalid code generation,
crash or Stage0/Stage1 semantic difference immediately preempts optimization. Budget exhaustion
must remain an explicit unknown. Never increase speed or coverage by dropping obligations,
weakening negative controls, adding assumptions, or bypassing independent replay.

### 23.27.3 Priority 0 — enforce Global.Read and Global.Write end to end

**Why now:** accepted unauthorized global mutation is a concrete semantic boundary failure;
one canonical fix protects every client of the compiler and proof assistant.

1. Qualify the compiler-owned grant checker through Stage0 and Stage1, including reporter and
   imported-method paths, using a matching compiler/runtime pair.
2. Require Global.Read for value reads of global mutable variables and Global.Write for writes.
   Read-modify-write requires both. Signature effect rows are optional inferred contracts, not body
   authorization: place local grants tightly around actual accesses/calls, with grouped family members
   such as `Global{Read,Write}`. Local `can` retains and propagates effects; `trusted` suppresses only
   deliberately covered effects. Preserve correct local/parameter/branch shadowing and enforce
   explicit grants through direct calls, forward calls, callbacks and imports.
3. Make both CLI and direct proof APIs fail closed on mandatory grant diagnostics before admitting
   certificates. Preserve diagnostic storage ownership across semantic-result export.
4. Migrate proof implementation globals with truthful grants or explicit context state. Avoid a
   blanket trusted bypass; favor eliminating ambient mutable modes where the change is cohesive.
5. Validate source-to-proof effect correspondence and independent replay at the trust boundary.

**Done when:** positive and missing/wrong-grant controls pass on all applicable entry routes;
unauthorized inputs publish no verified declarations or certificates; compiler stages agree;
the proof implementation builds with enforced grants; focused regressions and fresh replay pass.

### 23.27.4 Priority 1 — close proven replay and kernel trust gaps

**Why next:** existing reproducible failures offer more return than new tactics, and kernel errors
can invalidate every performance result.

1. Finish and integrate the narrow widening repair. Authenticate builtin cast identity by actual
   source expression, type and dispatch; an unrelated call sharing a position must retain mutation
   effects. Keep changed-initializer and custom-method controls.
2. Close loop/source witness authentication gaps, including removed original traces, renamed
   witnesses, edited invariants, owner identity, shadowing and rebinding. Reconstruct source-owned
   identity where retained-trace consistency is insufficient.
3. Triage the remaining failures by shared root cause and affected obligations: source accounting,
   fact/source binding, call frames, package correspondence, exception/region/borrow semantics.
   Investigate the six unverified standalone kernel declarations with explicit remaining assumptions.
4. Maintain strict malformed-package, cyclic-DAG, dependency, resource-limit and trust-state
   rejection. Extend adversarial tests around repaired boundaries rather than inventing broad
   new test infrastructure.

**Done per fix:** genuine source proves and independently replays; source/certificate mutations
reject; omitted obligations cannot disappear from reports; failures remain explicit; the fix
has a small commit with exact provenance and relevant regression results.

### 23.27.5 Priority 2 — establish a complete, actionable qualification baseline

**Why now:** a reliable complete ledger prevents repeated investigation and misleading success
claims. Run this alongside focused repairs when product identities are stable.

1. Build one coherent current producer/replay pair; verify publication, provenance and ABI gates.
2. With the repaired continued-test driver, run every ordered test part, including parts 10 onward,
   and retain terminal status and per-part reachability.
3. Classify failures by root cause, affected declarations and trust severity; distinguish outdated
   expectations and harness faults from semantic failures without weakening assertions.
4. Choose the next repair from this ledger, favoring common causes with multiple downstream failures.
   Rerun affected gates after each fix; repeat the entire matrix at integration checkpoints.

**Done when:** every part has a recorded outcome, failures are attributable and reproducible,
kernel/source/replay acceptance gates pass, and source/product identities match. A completed failing
matrix is useful evidence; it is not release qualification.

### 23.27.6 Priority 3 — optimize measured common-path user time

**Start gate:** trustworthy current products and a semantic baseline for the measured workloads.
Safe measurement and profiling can proceed while unrelated failures are being repaired.

Measure edit → build → check → inspect → export → fresh replay on pinned small, typical, large
and near-limit workloads. Include cold/warm and no-op/incremental cases. Record paired raw samples,
order, wall/CPU p50/p95, variability, peak RSS, work counters, compiler/runtime/product identity,
and exact obligation, assumption, certificate, trust and replay projections.

Choose **one** bottleneck from evidence, in this default order:

1. Avoid redundant product builds and unchanged dependency work while preserving coherent pair
   publication and complete invalidation.
2. Remove repeated source/owner/fact scans with bounded indexes and shared immutable analysis.
3. Reduce context copying, normalization and certificate-DAG traversal shown expensive by profiles.
4. Reuse checked artifacts only with exact source, dependency, semantic-mode, kernel and ABI identity.
   Independently replay persisted certificates initially; never trust a cached proven bit.
5. Reduce allocation and memory traffic; parallelize only after immutable ownership and deterministic
   cancellation/result semantics are established.

**Done per optimization:** paired representative results show useful whole-workflow savings with
identical semantic/trust projections and fresh replay. Report unchanged or slower cases and the
rollback condition. Same-binary calibration, isolated microbenchmarks and unmeasured changes do
not establish a speedup.

### 23.27.7 Priority 4 — expand useful coverage only from demonstrated demand

After higher gates, select the most frequent unresolved real-source class from the refreshed census:
for example loop/frame summaries, collections, aliases, arithmetic or exception/region paths.
Deliver one vertical slice: typed source semantics, complete obligation inventory, producer,
independent replay, refusal controls, diagnostics and measured cost.

Defer speculative theories, broad tactic expansion, interface polish, new protocol surfaces,
large rewrites, solver replacement and unprofiled micro-optimizations unless they directly unblock
a higher-ranked gate. Kernel dogfooding remains assurance work; count opaque helpers, compiler and
runtime assumptions explicitly.

### 23.27.8 Audit-driven assurance gates and controlling priority order

The supplied ChatGPT audit is a source/evidence review of compiler `fb97c5b2` and proof
`d8716191`, not an executed qualification. Its observation of the older proof compiler pin
does not describe every subsequent experiment. The newer focused repairs above establish only
their recorded scopes; they do not establish the assurance chain identified by the audit.
Treat source-inspected weaknesses as findings to reproduce, with current-source status and
positive/adversarial evidence recorded before claiming closure.

This ordering controls the queue above. Keep the concrete Global and replay repairs, but place
them within these release gates. Optimize within a qualified subset; do not defer trust-boundary
repairs in order to improve timings.

| Order | Highest-ROI deliverable | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Strict verified-build admission and authentic runtime privileges, including Global.Read/Write. | All required obligations block verified acceptance when unresolved; comment/string/import/environment spoof controls cannot grant application runtime privilege; CLI and direct APIs agree. |
| 1 | Complete independent source correspondence for one useful, explicitly defined subset. | Independently reconstructed source obligation inventory equals the required inventory; omitted, duplicated, stale and wrongly owned evidence rejects, including transitive dependencies. |
| 2 | Precise kernel semantics and rule soundness foundation. | Documented typed logic and machine/state/resource interpretation; explicit per-rule soundness arguments and mechanically checked results where available; adversarial independent replay remains mandatory. |
| 3 | Evidence bound to the exact delivered program and its assumptions. | Source, dependency, compiler, runtime, target, flags and executable identities are recorded; checked lowering or translation validation covers the selected subset. |
| 4 | Qualification, measured performance and demand-driven coverage. | Complete matrix outcomes, representative equivalent-workload measurements, and a vertical-slice coverage census with unsupported cases explicitly refused. |

#### Gate 0: distinguish compilation, runtime checking and verification

Ordinary compilation success is not verified-build success. Inventory every required obligation
across contracts, refinements, loop invariants, decreases, arithmetic safety, effects, resources
and proof construction. A strict verified mode must reject unresolved required obligations,
proof holes, unsupported reachable constructs and incomplete replay, regardless of whether the
ordinary compiler assigns an error, warning or note. Track obligations by stable source ownership
and kind; do not implement the policy solely as a severity-1 filter.

Retain separate reported assurance outcomes for ordinary compiled code, code with runtime checks,
and code meeting the strict verified policy. A runtime trap does not prove trap freedom.
The direct-API hard-diagnostic repair is necessary admission work, but does not by itself implement
this full verified policy. Add negative controls for each warning/note obligation class and for
reachable unsupported code, with zero publication as verified after any blocking outcome.

Reproduce the audited runtime-selection behavior in
`src/driver/elisac_source_probes.elisa`: the raw `def arena_alloc(` probe and
`ELISA_STAGE1_RUNTIME_STD` path reportedly select unit-wide runtime treatment, while affected
local grant checks return early. Record the actual bypass scope on the newest compiler.
Replace textual or ambient selection with per-declaration authenticated runtime provenance and
an explicit externally controlled trust manifest. Runtime imports must not upgrade adjacent
application declarations. Test comments, strings, forged declarations, mixed runtime/application
units, imports and environment selection through applicable compiler stages and proof APIs.
Coordinate this compiler-owned work with the compiler agent.

#### Gate 1: prove all required source obligations exist

Define a useful initial subset around pure scalar functions, contracts and refinements, then admit
additional constructs only with complete semantics and independent reconstruction. Publish a
capability matrix: admitted, conditionally assumed, runtime checked, or rejected. The source
checker must establish both that every required obligation was generated and that each was proved;
checking only the producer's supplied list is insufficient.

Prioritize transitive calls and dependencies, branch/state hypotheses, local mutation, exception
paths, arithmetic failure and termination before broader tactic support. Include stale mutable
collection facts, alias/frame changes, removed obligations and unsupported reachable callees in
adversarial controls. Producer adapters remain trusted until independent correspondence covers
their behavior; a valid kernel inference does not authenticate its source hypotheses.
Extend one complete vertical slice at a time, preserving explicit refusal outside it.

#### Gate 2: separate kernel implementation checking from logical soundness

Specify types, inference judgments, fixed-width arithmetic, state transitions and resource limits.
State the target theorem precisely: accepting a derivation of H entails C implies that every
interpretation satisfying H satisfies C under the stated semantics. Account for each rule,
normalization step and trusted helper, and identify which claims have formal proof, review,
testing or only an assumption.

Continue kernel dogfooding, malformed/cyclic package controls and independent replay, but report
these as implementation assurance. Self-verification does not establish logical soundness or
remove compiler/runtime assumptions; avoid circular justification. Use the existing helper
inventory to prioritize the smallest shared trusted components first.

#### Gate 3: connect source evidence to the executable

Bind the strict verification result to exact sources and dependency closure, specification,
compiler/runtime digests, target widths, build flags, lowering/optimization choices and executable
digest. Record signed overflow/trap versus wrapping behavior and allocation/runtime assumptions.
Bootstrap fixpoints and Stage0/Stage1 agreement are engineering evidence, not semantic preservation.

For the initial subset, pursue checked lowering or translation validation with independently
checked obligations; do not wait for a proof of the whole compiler. An executable provenance
manifest establishes identity, not correctness of compilation. Mark FFI contracts as conditional
assumptions until their implementations are verified. Keep concurrency, external scheduling and
liveness claims outside the admitted subset until their semantics and evidence are supported.

#### Gate 4: qualify useful guarantees and then expand

The first professional milestone is an explicitly defined Elisa subset with complete independently
checked evidence, visible assumptions, meaningful functional specifications, and trap-freedom and
termination/liveness guarantees where claimed. Proving a weak specification does not establish
absence of bugs. Publish the exact guarantee per declaration and delivered product.

Run the complete current matrix and maintain the shared-root-cause ledger alongside these gates.
Prioritize verified libraries and real workloads over full dependent types or speculative theories.
Collections/frames/aliases, aggregates/views/references, machine arithmetic/floats and concurrency
are separate coverage milestones requiring complete source semantics and replay. Measure performance
only with unchanged obligation and assurance projections; keep the original Lean 4/Dafny/F*
comparison objective, without claiming parity from narrow results.

### 23.27.9 Execution cadence and professional-performance gate

**Next sequence:** reproduce runtime privilege selection and finish canonical Global/direct-API
admission → implement strict required-obligation policy → close narrow replay defects and establish
complete correspondence for the initial useful subset → integrate on the newest coherent
compiler/runtime and complete the all-part ledger → formalize kernel semantics/rules and bind
delivered-product evidence, with checked lowering for that subset → measure and optimize its
largest common-path cost → expand the highest-demand supported source class. Kernel modeling,
qualification and safe measurement may overlap with admission work. Do not build against a
compiler/runtime pair while another agent is replacing it.

Per change: reproduce → select owning layer → make a cohesive fix → run meaningful positive and
adversarial gates → verify source accounting/trust → fresh replay → measure if performance-related →
commit only validated work → update evidence and this queue. Keep unrun gates explicit.

Professional-level claims require a representative supported-source corpus, reproducible complete
qualification, independent adversarial kernel testing, bounded failure behavior, and transparent
remaining assumptions. Compare end-to-end latency, throughput, resource use and verified coverage
with Lean 4/Dafny/F* only on explicitly comparable tasks, versions and hardware. Do not infer broad
parity from one workload or successful self-verification.

### 23.27.102 Result-symbol provenance and loop-preservation replay follow-up (2026-10-11; supersedes §23.27.101 replay draft)

This entry supersedes §23.27.101's replay-draft assessment and next step; its separate compiler
consolidation notes remain current. The active source draft extends the result-symbol type-bound
path for locals initialized by a direct call. It now requires a unique source declaration,
matching declared-local and callee return widths, and at least one source-validated
`local == result_symbol` alias at its declaration. Identical trace records for that one source
fact are allowed; conflicting local-binding or
summary uses fail closed. Source alias validation checks the exact call site and local reaching
definition at the binding line. The call-result symbol must also be available in the consumer
state: either its local alias is live at the consumer, or its marker is a fact in a loop-header
preservation certificate whose sourced guard/invariant and self-update reconstruct the post-body
invariant goal. Function-summary results that use the same internal symbol go through this
availability check when a certificate consumes them. The consumer must identify the unique source
loop header; break/continue certificates are tied to their transfer lines. Because the report
identifies consumers by line without a column, result-symbol availability is refused when its
declaration shares the consumer line; this prevents an inline transfer from bypassing the
loop-header phase check through ordinary alias liveness. Consumers whose line falls inside the
call initializer's source span are also refused, covering multiline recovery transfers nested in
call arguments.

The focused harness includes controls for removing the alias trace, shifting its source line,
removing consumer-certificate context, replacing the preservation goal with the entry invariant
while keeping context rows, and preserving a later call bound on normal fallthrough after a
`GetElse` continue while refusing that context when relabeled to the transfer line. The GetElse
check swaps source text into an already-built report; it exercises replay source-gating with the
normal header certificate, not a fresh parse, proof check, or producer-generated continue
certificate for that variant. The existing source-binding harness now also mutates a valid
preservation attempt and its certificate to an unrecognized phase and requires the general
attempt matcher to reject the pair; this mutation control has not been run on Stage1. The
function-summary consumer path still needs direct regression coverage. Context-free call-site
inspection stays available for source validation, while certificate consumption must pass the
result-symbol availability check. Ordinary local type-bound witness scope remains a
separate static audit item: source declaration uniqueness currently does not prove that a local
binding is available at the consuming certificate.
`git diff --check` and Python AST parsing pass, and
`type_bound_validation.elisa` remains 591 lines. No Stage1 compile or replay harness run has been
performed: the shared compiler lane has not been released. Keep this candidate explicitly
unverified and do not count the certificate-10 replay gap as closed until the same pinned-product
compile, adversarial controls, and focused replay pass.

### 23.27.1391 Guard lexical call-result availability at joins

The current resource-history implementation keeps newly executed call roots local to a branch or
nested scope. This prevents a post-join result marker from re-resolving a call against bindings
different from those used when it ran; only the inherited call-root prefix survives, while the
separate duplicate-execution history still records child calls. Updated the kernel inventory
regression to require this fail-closed lexical rule. Safe recovery of call results shared across
branches would need explicit proof that the relevant binding environment agrees on every path.
The kernel inventory, resource-summary cache guard, diff check, and source-length gate pass. Runtime
resource regressions remain unqualified because the installed proof binary does not match this
source tree.

### 23.27.127 Generic alias scope and lookup parity (2026-10-12)

The conversion classifier now checks caller generic binders only while reading the caller's type
syntax. When it expands a separately declared alias body, producer and replay disable caller-scope
generic shadowing, preserving valid intrinsic classification when an alias's global type name happens
to match a caller generic name. Producer generic binders now use the same bounded `(line, name)`
open-addressed index and duplicate counts as replay instead of scanning all generic rows per lookup.
Alias lookup remains source-work metered; `git diff --check` and the 600-line source gate pass. No
Elisa build, tests, replay, or timing was run; source-matched compiler qualification remains open.

### 23.27.128 Drop-analysis scope and alias lookup (2026-10-12)

Drop-risk traversal now carries the owning declaration line through expressions and statements.
Field-conversion checks and local type checks can therefore resolve caller generic binders in their
own scope. The callable index retains each function or callable extern's declaration line, so a
uniquely resolved call's return type is checked against the callee's generic scope. Producer and
structural replay share the same collection path.

Producer and structural replay now compute the same root-alias visibility result from their source
snapshot before drop analysis. Aliases are kept opaque when imports or visibility-changing
annotations make bare-name resolution uncertain, so an imported type cannot be classified through
a same-named root alias. With visibility proven safe, conversion analysis retains non-generic
module alias bodies for qualified lookup; the drop classifier keeps a separate root-only target
table so unqualified drop analysis cannot follow a module alias by spelling alone. Fixed-point drop
analysis keeps a source-work-metered list of root-owned structs and enums and treats a nominal as
no-drop only when its spelling is unique, the root list contains it once, visibility is safe, and no
alias has the same name. Runtime drop analysis applies the corresponding owner-row check after
conversion indexes are built. Module-owned names, collisions, aliases, and uncertain visibility stay
potentially dropping.

Drop-type fixed-point expansion now builds temporary bounded hash indexes for alias, declared, and
root-declared names, plus a dynamically growing bounded hash set for destructor-hook membership.
Alias-target, owner-aware nominal, and hook membership lookups reuse those indexes across alias and
declaration scans instead of repeatedly traversing the name vectors. Hook seeds are collected in a
linear pass and deduplicated through the same set before fixed-point expansion. The completed hook
set is also installed in a persistent bounded name index for runtime effect classification. Index
construction, growth, rehashes, and probes consume the existing source-work budget; duplicate names
and malformed lookup states remain fail-closed. The successful alias index is reused by the later
conversion-index build after constant-time shape checks, avoiding a duplicate unscoped build while
retaining the scoped indexes needed for type-conversion analysis.

Generic-shadow lookup in the drop fixed point now uses the persistent bounded indexes keyed by name
and `(declaration-line, name)`, built once before expansion and reused by conversion and replay after
constant-time validity and shape checks. The old per-leaf scan of all generic rows and duplicate
temporary index construction are removed, reducing expected work from O(G*T) to O(G+T). Construction,
probes, cluster checks, and query text remain source-work metered, and malformed index states fail
closed, including positive counts whose capacity calculation overflows to zero. The constant-time
reuse checks validate flags and shapes, not index contents; this relies on producer index reset before
source refresh and replay's fresh scratch cache. Any future in-place generic-row mutation must
invalidate both persistent indexes. Its performance impact is unmeasured; source-matched
qualification remains open.

Drop-risk classifiers have since been factored into `src/proof/check/drop_type_index.elisa`;
`implicit_effect_guard.elisa` is 388 lines and `drop_type_index.elisa` is 344, both below the
600-line cap. `mutable_local_bindings.elisa` is now 531 lines. The latest
`scripts/check_source_length.py`, `git diff --check`, and `git diff --cached --check` runs pass. No

### 23.27.153 Qualified transitive deterministic-call precision (2026-10-12)

Static audit of deterministic-call replay confirmed a conservative precision gap: the source walker
retains transitive callees only as leaf names, and recursive replay therefore requires a globally
unique declaration group even when the AST contained a qualified module path. The initial traced
qualified call does retain and validate its full path and owner. Preserving qualified path ASTs and
resolving each transitive edge with the report-local module-alias index could admit valid repeated
leaf names without weakening ambiguity handling, but this requires an AST-carrying edge representation
through the bounded walker and recursion stack. No code change was made pending that broader refactor;
current false rejection is documented, with no wrong-owner acceptance identified by static review.

Const-enum replay now reconstructs the exact declaration path for qualified nominal enum types,
including nested module names that the parser stores as fully qualified paths. It also follows the
producer's unique bare-alias chain before checking the target declaration, while retaining every
alias spelling for `Eq` override checks. Producer and replay still require a globally unique leaf
name for the enum aggregate, so same-named enums in unrelated modules remain conservatively
rejected. A qualified `Module::Alias` whose alias is declared in that module is also still rejected:
the current alias lookup is leaf-based and cannot prove the alias owner's scope. Module aliases and
imports require their own source-backed path mapping rather than treating their spellings as
declaration paths. These remaining cases need a shared bounded type-path resolver over owner paths,
used symmetrically by the producer and replay.

The enum replay source-tree walk, enum path resolver, and member lookup now share the producer's
64-level type-audit depth bound; variant-case recursion retains its separate 32-level bound.
Builtin operator type recognition also rejects source declarations that shadow its builtin names.

The existing conversion resolver is a useful implementation reference but is not directly
interchangeable with enum witness resolution: it has caller generic checks and conversion-specific
builtin/nominal rules, and its replay form depends on a populated `ProofReplayCallSiteTarget` built
from a source-derived effect index. A sound witness fix needs a small shared, bounded type-path
resolver over declaration owner paths that can distinguish nominal declarations from aliases,
follow alias RHSs in their declaring module, preserve each alias spelling for operator-override
checks, and be independently reconstructed by replay. Reuse of the conversion helper should wait
until those differences are explicit in the API.

### 23.27.154 Shared-budget congruence operand reads (2026-10-12)

The congruence replay path now charges the shared goal-search budget before its operand collection,

checks, and exhaustion stops the congruence attempt. `git diff --check` and
`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No Elisa build, tests, replay, or timing were run.

### 23.27.155 Report-level admissibility requires completeness (2026-10-12)

The checked-view report-level admissibility gate now also requires `source_complete`. Previously a

queryable, but overall report actions now fail closed on incomplete source admission or obligations.
Static whitespace and source-length checks pass; no Elisa build, CLI run, or tests were run.

### 23.27.267 Module-local source conversion alias RHS resolution (2026-10-12)

Source conversion alias expansion now resolves bare alias names in a non-root alias RHS against

No Elisa build, tests, or replay were run, so compiler qualification remains open.

### 23.27.156 Dogfood immutable product-pair handoff (2026-10-12)

Dogfood now receives the checksum-verified proof/replay pair as JSON from `build.sh` while the

and portable package export/replay, including cache-hit builds, and honors the configured
generation root. The invalid handoff-mode guard runs before lock acquisition so a bad invocation
cannot strand the build lock. The existing static guard now checks the handoff protocol and guard
ordering. Shell syntax, Python syntax, source length, and whitespace checks pass. No dogfood run or
source-matched proof qualification was performed.

### 23.27.157 Metered variant-exclusion source walks (2026-10-12)

Variant-exclusion producer scans now share the report's source-work budget while counting enum

remain ineligible, and variant/condition comparisons are charged before recursive work. Pairwise
exclusions now cover enums with more than eight variants; repeated subject terms and generated
clause structure are charged, while the separate match-exhaustiveness disjunction retains its
eight-case cap and only stores enough variants to reject over-cap cases. `git diff --check` and
`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No Elisa build, tests, replay, or timing were run.

### 23.27.158 Meter float-type alias scans to shared source work (2026-10-12)

The float-parameter audit now charges expression nodes, type-name de-duplication comparisons,

checker fallback. Exhaustion or an unrecognized type expression remains conservatively
float-possible; exhaustion also marks the shared source counter over limit so report admission
fails closed. `git diff --check` and `scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No Elisa build, tests, or
replay were run.

### 23.27.159 Metered match-exhaustiveness replay expression walks (2026-10-12)

Match-exhaustiveness replay now charges each AST node visit in both its case-count pass and its

`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No Elisa build, tests, or replay were run.

### 23.27.160 Indexed wide condition-alias intersections (2026-10-12)

True/false alias-set intersections now use a temporary exact-name hash index when both paths have

No Elisa build, tests, or replay were run.

### 23.27.161 Source-bound character pattern facts (2026-10-12)

Typed pattern facts now recover the narrow character literal subset already preserved by the

No prover run or build was performed because the available proof/compiler products are not matched

The proof-language float gate now follows enum payload field types, including aliases to enums,

### 23.27.166 Conservative mutable-reference markers at depth exhaustion (2026-10-12)

Generic receipt completeness, attempt status, certificate status, and batched status snapshots now

### 23.27.169 Respect local shadowing in const-enum qualification (2026-10-12)

Const-enum body qualification now carries visible parameter, sequential local, assignment, and

### 23.27.170 Scope replay generic shadow checks to the active function (2026-10-12)

Replay's conversion-alias generic check now requires the supplied generic-owner line to match the

### 23.27.171 Scope producer generic checks across encoded-range lines (2026-10-12)

Producer conversion and drop-type generic-shadow lookups now use exact `(line, name)` rows even
when a source `#line` value has the high bit set. An encoded generic-bound row can only add a
conservative shadow match to an exact query. Ownerless file-wide queries use a name index that
excludes bound rows, so they now fail incomplete if any high-bit row makes it impossible to know
whether that row is a source binder or encoded bound. This prevents a missing shadow check while
retaining precise high-line lookups when the active declaration owner is known. The lexer accepts
directive digits without a `2^31` cap, while `Ast::File` snapshots preserve only parallel
line/name arrays, not a row-kind discriminator. `git diff --check` and
`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No build, tests, or replay were run.

Build manifests, cached manifests, Stage1 provenance records, and proof/replay pair manifests now

### 23.27.268 Extend const-enum qualification through scoped proof expressions (2026-10-12)

Const-enum member qualification now follows common call, index, collection, refinement, and

### 23.27.176 Index validated structural certificate owners (2026-10-12)

Structural replay already grouped certificates by owner in a hash index, but cached validated
owners in a separate linear array. Repeated certificates across many structural functions could
therefore spend quadratic work merely checking whether an owner had already been rederived. The

certificate set matches the source rederivation. This keeps the reuse check on the existing
bounded hash lookup and the cache remains local to one replay batch. `git diff --check` and
`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No tests, build, or replay were run.

### 23.27.177 Precompute ownerless generic-line ambiguity (2026-10-12)

Ownerless source type-alias queries conservatively refuse if any generic side-table row has a

ambiguity check previously rescanned all generic rows on every query. Generic-index construction
now records the condition once, reset with the other source indexes, and queries use the flag in

`scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No tests, build, or replay were run.

### 23.27.180 Revoke certificate replay when whole-arena admission fails (2026-10-12)

Certificate batching recorded a failed whole-arena admission but still attempted certificates;

per row. `git diff --check` and `scripts/check_source_length.py` pass. No tests, build, or replay
were run.

Structural-safety replay now resolves a unique owner and callee from the retained declaration tree,

The direct API harness now starts with a source-checked report and a valid whole kernel arena, then

Membership typing previously compared a value's family and spelling against a container's element

contextual numeric conversions for numeric membership. Static whitespace and source-size checks pass;
nominal collision and numeric conversion controls remain for runtime qualification after the hold.

### 23.27.350 Scope remaining declaration marker queries to their owner (2026-10-13)

The final two marker-summary callers with known declaration owners still selected the ownerless,
file-wide generic-name fallback: old-parameter witnesses and qualified-constant witnesses. Both now
pass the active function declaration line and use the existing line-indexed binder lookup, so an
unrelated same-named generic no longer shadows the queried type. Ownerless fallback remains available
only for genuinely ownerless callers. `git diff --check` and source-length checks pass; Elisa runtime
qualification remains under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.351 Preserve typed-term recursion bounds across reference classification (2026-10-13)

Reference and raw-pointer classifiers used the top-level term-sort wrapper when they encountered a
call, field, or scope. That wrapper reset both depth and remaining recursion allowance to the root
budget. Typed term sorting calls back into those classifiers for call arguments and compound values,
so a deeply nested serialized term could repeatedly restart the per-path stack bound. The classifiers
now accept the active depth, pass it through recursive branches, and call the remaining-budget sorter
instead of resetting through the wrapper. Cross-classifier descent also stops when no child budget
remains, preserving the sorter's positive-remaining precondition. The serialized-node validity
predicate only checks the root index, so node construction provides no stronger depth invariant.
Static source inspection, `git diff --check`, and source-length checks pass; parser/build/replay
remain held.

### 23.27.352 Index reference-parameter annotations by declaration line and name (2026-10-13)

Kernel signature construction previously rescanned every `__typestate_ref_param` annotation for each
function and then linearly searched that function's names for each formal. Added one report-local,
open-addressed `(line, parameter-name)` index with exact collision checks and the shared cluster cap.
Index construction is linear in the annotation count; each formal now uses a bounded lookup. Duplicate
annotations retain their previous Boolean-membership behavior. Index build or probe exhaustion fails
closed. `git diff --check` and source-length checks pass; runtime qualification remains under the
static-only hold.

### 23.27.353 Deduplicate tuple container descriptors by bounded identity index (2026-10-13)

The tuple-field source walk searched the entire accumulated typing-binding array for each inferred
container descriptor, producing quadratic work as container types accumulated. The source type index
now owns a fixed-capacity open-addressed descriptor-identity table sized from the global binding cap.
Each container expression identity is inserted once; repeated identities compare the full descriptor
sort before reuse. Epoch tags separate global bindings from each proposition's fresh local binding
array, so a hit never reuses a row offset from another array; advancing the epoch avoids clearing the
fixed table for every proposition. Descriptor insertion and exact comparisons consume source-work,
and cluster, shape, or binding-cap exhaustion fails closed. `git diff --check` and source-length
checks pass; parser, build, and replay remain under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.354 Keep cast-shaped scalar witnesses opaque until dispatch is verified (2026-10-13)

Typed proposition replay now admits method-shaped numeric and const-enum casts only when the
environment has no visible matching `__cast__` hook. Ordinary functions with a cast-selector name
do not shadow method-shaped cast syntax in the pinned compiler. The scalar witness path
previously trusted an exact primitive-scalar marker before inspecting cast syntax, and the unsigned
widening rewrite erased a cast call into its receiver. Both paths now refuse to treat integer cast
selectors as ordinary scalar witnesses or strip them during either active metered or compatibility
widening. This is conservative and may reduce cast-related proof automation until dispatch evidence
is threaded through those APIs. Static diff and source-length checks pass; runtime qualification
remains under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.355 Preserve compiler-wide cast-hook lookup (2026-10-13)

Kernel typed-term replay scans a declaration-wide environment, which includes functions from
nested modules. Pinned compiler inspection confirmed that the cast-hook index scans its shared
function table without filtering module owners, so an exact sibling-module hook can win dispatch.
The attempted module-prefix filter was removed; replay checks every complete hook for an exact
source/target pair and fails closed for any incomplete `__cast__` metadata. Separate source-boundary
cast checks remain file-wide because their trace metadata does not yet preserve a reliable module
owner; they remain conservative and can suppress proofs in files containing unrelated hooks.
Static checks pass; runtime qualification remains held.

### 23.27.356 Do not treat cast-selector function names as method dispatch (2026-10-13)

Typed local-initializer replay and fact-call snapshots rejected builtin cast proofs when any source
function or extern had the same name as the numeric cast selector. The pinned compiler gives scalar
cast syntax precedence over ordinary UFCS selectors, so these name checks and the producer's
numeric-selector shadow table were unnecessary false refusals and are removed. Type-bound replay
also no longer looks up an ordinary function by selector name. The broader `__cast__` refusal
remains wherever replay lacks exact pair or module-visibility evidence. A positive ordinary/extern
selector fixture is registered in the cast-dispatch gate. Static checks pass; runtime qualification
remains under the hold.

### 23.27.357 Fail closed on unresolved imports in structural source graphs (2026-10-13)

Structural call-graph reconstruction treated a source call with no retained declaration match as
non-recursive and did not account for `Decl.Import` or import/using annotation metadata. An
imported callable could therefore be omitted from reachability. Structural graph construction now
refuses declaration imports and unresolved import/using markers before building the graph; those
walks charge the source-work budget. This is deliberately conservative until reports carry
resolved import targets and selected-callee identities. Direct-API mutation coverage now injects
both an import declaration and `__using` metadata after source checking, and requires structural
replay to retain a gap. `git diff --check` and source-length checks pass; parser/build/replay remain
under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.358 Reuse the bounded callable-name index in structural checking (2026-10-13)

Structural termination repeatedly scanned every function name while checking whether parameters,
pattern binders, or expression identifiers could shadow callable names. The checker now snapshots
the already-built bounded function-name hash table into structural metadata once, and uses exact-name
lookups with the existing cluster cap and source-work meter. An unavailable or malformed index and
any exhausted lookup fail closed. This removes a repeated full-name scan from each shadow check;
no throughput improvement has been measured. `git diff --check` and source-length checks pass;
parser/build/replay qualification remains held until the proof source and compiler product match.

### 23.27.359 Reuse precomputed SCC labels in structural termination (2026-10-13)

Structural initialization rebuilt component labels by comparing each function with all earlier
functions, despite the function pass already producing `recursive_component_ids`. It also ran a
per-function scan to populate a mutual-member flag that had no readers. Structural initialization
now validates and copies the existing row-aligned SCC labels once, charging validation and copy
work; malformed arrays or labels leave the component table empty, and structural checking refuses
that shape. This changes SCC metadata transfer from quadratic comparisons to a linear pass and
removes the dead scan. `git diff --check` and the source-length gate pass. Elisa runtime behavior
remains unqualified under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.360 Recheck checked-view proof-status boundaries (2026-10-13)

Static inspection confirms `ProofCheckedView` keeps its report, receipt, and parser-origin source
analysis private; its constructor is private, and `proof_checked_view_attempt_is_proven` requires
both replay status and per-goal source admission. Standalone `proof_replay_certificates` returns
an unbound receipt; its `kernel_*` accessors are diagnostic, while source-authorized accessors
require a source-bound validated receipt. CLI and output serializers consume the checked view and
report replay and source admission separately. No mutable-report admission bypass was found in
these routes. This does not authenticate direct inspection of the legacy raw report API and is
static inspection only; runtime qualification remains under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.361 Index repeated function declarations by name and line (2026-10-13)

`proof_function_index_at_line` previously scanned all function rows whenever a bare name was
ambiguous, making repeated declaration checks potentially quadratic. Function-index construction
now builds a secondary open-addressed `(name, declaration line)` index containing only rows with a
repeated bare name and an aligned line. Hash matches still require exact name and line equality;
unique pairs resolve to their row, while absent pairs and duplicate exact pairs preserve the old
`names.count` sentinel behavior. Build, lookup, and cluster work use the shared source-work bound;
incomplete lookup state marks module-resolution work exhausted so callers fail closed. Static diff
and source-length checks pass. Runtime behavior and throughput remain unqualified under the
static-only hold.

### 23.27.362 Clarify raw report completion versus source admission (2026-10-13)

`proof_report_source_has_unresolved_checks` accepts a raw mutable `ProofReport` and has no replay
receipt or parser-origin source capability. Its false result therefore describes report invariants
and producer-marked obligation closure only. Added this distinction at the public helper and in the
README; source-positive decisions use `ProofCheckedView` and its `proof_checked_view_source_admissible`
accessor with replay status. This is a documentation boundary clarification, not a change to raw
report behavior or a new runtime qualification.

### 23.27.363 Reuse the bounded extern-signature index in proof analysis (2026-10-13)

Effect containment, operator-witness analysis, and resource-call classification repeatedly scanned
all extern signatures to resolve a name. They now probe the already-built extern name index with
exact string equality after hash matches; missing and duplicate extern names retain the count
sentinel. Probe and comparison work is charged to the shared implicit-effect budget, and malformed
index state or exhaustion refuses the analysis. Static diff and source-length checks pass; runtime
behavior and throughput remain unqualified under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.364 Index expected source-call sets during replay matching (2026-10-13)

The production source-call collector already deduplicates names with a bounded, collision-safe
index, but its call-set matcher compared every collected name against every expected name and then
rescanned the expected prefix to detect duplicates. Replay now indexes expected names once and uses
exact string comparison after hash matches; duplicate expected names and malformed, over-clustered,
or over-budget indexes fail closed. Final effect-trace validation calls the production work-aware
matcher with source annotations and the shared source-work counter. The older unmetered
`source_call_walk` remains example-only. Static diff and source-length checks pass; runtime behavior
remains unqualified under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.365 Share the source-work budget across effect containment (2026-10-13)

Effect containment's extern identity, producer row/set work, and final trace validation consume the
same report-level source-work counter. Final validation performs the caller and callee source
lookups, call coverage, and effect-row binding once, avoiding duplicate preflight scans. Extern
metadata uses a metered identity variant. The producer uses bounded indexes to deduplicate declared
effects, callee rows, and call sets; cross-row comparisons receive checked work charges before
running. Budget exhaustion records a resource-analysis budget finding and a failed proof obligation,
while source mismatches retain opaque refusals. The replay call-work charge marks the shared counter
exhausted when a charge fails, so callers can distinguish exhaustion from a semantic mismatch.
Static diff and source-length checks pass; runtime behavior remains unqualified under the
static-only hold.

### 23.27.366 Keep effect-containment callee metadata aligned (2026-10-13)

The new bounded callee-name index appends each previously unseen name to `callee_names` during
insertion. Effect-containment production then appended the same name again after building its row,
while adding only one start/count entry. Trace construction iterates by `callee_names.count`, so even
one callee could index beyond the row metadata. Removed the second append; the name, row start, and
row count now each receive exactly one entry per unique callee. Static diff and source-length checks
pass; runtime qualification remains held.

### 23.27.367 Reuse typed-match call shape during overload selection (2026-10-13)

Each overload candidate that passed typed argument matching also passed the exact call-shape
matcher, but selection immediately scanned its labels, arity, and defaulted parameters a second
time. Typed matches now contribute to both the typed-match and shape-match counts directly;
type-mismatching candidates still run the shape-only fallback. This removes one redundant shape
scan per applicable candidate while retaining unique-shape fallback behavior. Static diff and
source-length checks pass; measured throughput and runtime parity remain unqualified under the
static-only hold.

### 23.27.368 Do not infer reference arguments from untyped numeric literals (2026-10-13)

The pinned backend's typed overload matcher contextually matches only direct untyped integer and
float literal AST nodes. `Paren` and `Move` preserve the unmodeled expression type but do not enter
that typed literal branch; only a unique call shape may then provide contextual typing during
emission. Replay previously unwrapped those forms to default `i64`/`f64` sorts and could count one
candidate in an otherwise ambiguous overload set. A bounded parenthesis/move-aware detector now
keeps wrapped literals out of typed ranking, preserves contextual typing in a unique-shape
fallback, and refuses untyped numeric literals for reference formals. Typed place arguments retain
their reference path subject to the source-shape guard recorded in 23.27.369. `git diff --check` and
source-length checks pass; replay qualification remains under the static-only hold.

### 23.27.369 Match unary literal overload fallback and reject literal borrows (2026-10-13)

Pinned compiler inspection confirmed that expression typing unwraps unary `+`, `-`, and `~`,
while typed overload matching still accepts contextual typing only for direct integer/float literal
AST nodes. Replay's bounded literal classifier now carries those unary forms out of typed candidate
ranking. A unique-shape fallback may contextualize unary `+`/`-` to numeric formals and `~` only to
integral formals. Explicit `&` is rejected for by-value formals and accepted for by-reference
formals only when a bounded, metered source-shape walk verifies an identifier, field, index,
parenthesized place, or a named struct call whose address is materialized by the pinned backend.
This excludes literals, arithmetic/call rvalues with scalar results, and nested borrows while
retaining ordinary ident/field/index places and backend-supported CStr index places.
`git diff --check` and source-length checks pass; runtime qualification remains under the
static-only hold.

### 23.27.370 Harden structural source-graph replay gaps (2026-10-13)

The structural source binding added in 23.27.130 is now hardened against source forms the replay
graph cannot resolve exactly. Graph construction fails closed on imports and unresolved
import/using annotations; name-index insertion and lookup stop at the shared cluster cap, and
lookup exhaustion no longer claims absence. Graph nodes remain keyed by exact source-entry
identity so unrelated overloads can coexist, while certificate owner/callee admission still
requires unique source declarations. Scoped, indirect, unresolved-dispatch, and non-callable
constant calls taint reachability instead of connecting to a same-leaf declaration. Structural
replay also requires the proof structural name index before graph-cache construction. These changes
are statically present in `structural_source_validation.elisa` and its import guard; no parser,
build, test, or replay qualification is available under the active hold.

### 23.27.371 Keep mutable-reference callables incomplete in proposition typing (2026-10-13)

`ProofKernelTypingBinding` records whether a formal is by-reference but not whether that
reference is mutable. Source proposition typing now resolves reference mutability through type
aliases and emits an incomplete callable signature whenever a formal is a mutable reference.
This prevents overload selection from treating `mutable T&` as `T&` while retaining shared
reference calls and mutable by-value parameters. The same bounded alias walk also supplies the
formal's by-reference bit for signature emission, avoiding repeated reference-classification scans.
Reference-parameter annotations are now validated in that preflight pass too. Every formal's
lookup-completeness and reference-versus-nullable-sort compatibility is checked and cached before
the checker emits either a complete signature or an incomplete-candidate marker, so a later bad
formal cannot leave a partial callable behind.
The source-level regression matrix in `scripts/test_mutable_reference_proposition_signatures.py`
rejects direct and aliased mutable-reference calls during proposition formation while keeping
shared-reference and mutable-by-value calls eligible. The matrix is registered in the Python suite
but has not run; runtime qualification remains under the hold. It does not synthesize malformed
internal `__typestate_ref_param` metadata. The new direct AST harness in
`scripts/test_mutable_reference_annotation_preflight.py` injects a mismatched marker on a later
formal and checks that projection emits only an incomplete signature, with no function or parameter
rows. It also checks a nullable-reference compatibility control and malformed reference-index
lookups that must publish no rows. Reserved `__typestate_ref_param` rows with an empty owner now
make index construction incomplete instead of silently disappearing. The harness is registered but
unrun under the hold. It now also projects successive `Left::Ref`, `Right::Ref`, and caller-local
`Node` formals and requires three distinct nominal identities, preserving the caller scope across
both alias walks. This scope-restoration control remains unrun under the hold. A future extension
can carry reference mutability through source typing and validate actual-place capabilities.

### 23.27.372 Check pattern-work capacity before adding source-name length (2026-10-13)

Pattern source lookup charged a type name by adding `1 + sview_len(name)` before checking the
work limit. The bound now compares the name length against remaining capacity first, so the
meter arithmetic cannot wrap before the refusal check. `git diff --check` and the source-length
gate pass; pattern regressions remain unrun under the exact-toolchain qualification hold.

### 23.27.373 Require exact pinned toolchain inputs in replay harnesses (2026-10-13)

The shared source-binding harness compared the compiler snapshot revision and standard library,
then checked only that the installed Stage1 matched its current checkout. That could still run
replay against a dirty or differently pinned compiler source tree. It now validates the Stage1
product, complete snapshot source tree, build recipe, and Stage0 seed chain against both checked-in
pins before compiling. Both replay harnesses compare every file in the canonical standard library
they actually use against the validated snapshot, so qualification covers the input consumed by
replay. The mutable-reference annotation harness now uses the same preflight, and its freshness
check cannot be bypassed with `ELISA_ALLOW_STALE_STAGE1=1`. This is a qualification guard only; the
current mismatched toolchain still prevents compiler or replay runs.

### 23.27.374 Fuse formal sort and reference-marker classification (2026-10-13)

Each formal parameter previously traversed its type AST and alias chain once for the replay sort,
then again to discover shared/mutable-reference markers. The sort walker now also returns
independent reference-marker fields, and formal preflight consumes both results from that single
walk. Sort-only callers keep their projection wrapper and do not request marker collection; formal
preflight requests both results. Alias lookup still recurses under the alias owner path and restores
the caller path; marker completeness remains separate from sort completeness, and annotation lookup
still runs for every formal before any callable rows are published. This removes duplicate span
charging and alias resolution on the signature hot path. Diff/whitespace and source-length checks
pass. The direct/shared/mutable/nullable/alias regression harnesses remain unrun under the
exact-toolchain static-only hold, so semantics and budget parity are not yet runtime-qualified.
Container element admission still performs a separate reference-shape check before its recursive
sort. Return signatures now use a demand-aware fused classifier as recorded in 23.27.380; its budget
and semantic parity remain unqualified under the exact-toolchain hold.

### 23.27.375 Cover additional numeric-looking string pattern spellings (2026-10-13)

The pattern-collision regression already exercised leading-zero decimal strings, Boolean/null
spellings, and fixed-width integer boundaries. It also includes hexadecimal-looking and
exponent-looking string pairs (`"0x1"`/`"1"` and `"1e0"`/`"1.0"`) in report, theorem, package,
and focused CLI checks. Those adversarial pairs must remain distinct string facts; their spellings
are now admitted as exact string facts only under authenticated `sview`/`cstr` scrutinee types.
Fixed-width integer patterns remain closed. The runtime assertions are not qualified by the
current proof product.

### 23.27.376 Exercise additional unsigned pattern widths (2026-10-13)

The fixed-width pattern collision matrix now exercises the high bit for `u16` and `u32` in
addition to the existing `u8` and `u64` cases, and the maximum `u64` literal separately from its
high bit. This checks that width-specific literal handling cannot create a false postcondition
proof at intermediate unsigned widths or at the unsigned maximum. The cases use the same report,
theorem, package, and focused CLI assertions as the other collisions. Python syntax,
`git diff --check`, and the source-length gate pass; runtime assertions remain unqualified under
the exact-toolchain hold.

### 23.27.377 Fail closed on unresolved formal marker lookup and precharge publication (2026-10-13)

The fused formal type classifier now marks reference-shape completeness false when a named-type
lookup has anything other than exactly one declaration, including an unresolved name. Before

and every formal row and precharges the corresponding source work. This keeps budget or binding

resource-accounting changes; the type-alias and signature regression harnesses remain unrun under

### 23.27.378 Preserve early refusal when considering return-classifier fusion (2026-10-13)

The initial static review found that a wholesale replacement of the reference-first return path

### 23.27.379 Keep owner-generic builtin spellings out of kernel source typing (2026-10-13)

The proposition type projector could classify a generic parameter named like a builtin (for

parser/build/replay regression remains unrun under the active exact-toolchain hold.

### 23.27.380 Fuse return sort and reference-marker classification with demand-aware traversal (2026-10-13)

Return signatures now collect sort and reference markers in the shared AST/alias classifier. The
classifier switches to marker-only recursion for direct reference wrappers, preserving early
incomplete-candidate admission without charging alias sort work. Exact nullable `T&?` results first
validate the reference shape, then retain a pointee sort because the nullable pointer is represented

checks remain prohibited until the exact-toolchain hold is lifted, so budget and semantic parity are

### 23.27.381 Refuse field projection through nullable receivers without a null refinement (2026-10-13)

Static replay review found that proposition typing looked up a field from the pointee type identity

Replay now returns an unknown sort for field projection through nullable and nullable-opaque

enum paths remain available. Static
whitespace, source-length, and diff checks pass. No runtime or regression test was run under the
exact-toolchain hold.

Further static review found that the one-segment `E.V` shadow check ran only after the specialized

### 23.27.405 Confirm Global.Write bypass through reference-bearing binders (2026-10-13)

Static audit of the pinned compiler authority pass confirmed an authorization gap, not just
missing descriptive metadata. A minimal candidate is a mutable global `box`, a helper that writes
through `mutable Box&`, and `for p in [&box]: set(p)` inside a function granted `Global.Read` only.
The pass walks the `&box` iterable as a read, seeds `p` with null type and no origin, recognizes
the helper's mutable formal, then calls `ga_write_place(p)`. Its local-name resolution returns no
global slot for `p`, so the caller can miss the required `Global.Write`; the callee sees only a
parameter and also cannot attribute the write to the global. The same origin loss occurs in match
arms and comprehension binders. These source paths were statically inspected in the pinned clean
compiler checkout; the candidate was not run because the Stage1/Stage0 provenance hold remains.

Repair should carry binder type and storage origin through `for`, comprehension, and match
projection. Retain exact global roots when derivable, merge origin sets across alternatives, and
fail closed for unresolved reference-capable aliases when a mutating call or place write uses them.
Scalar binders should remain untracked. Add paired granted/missing-write cases and qualify through
both CLI and proof API on a provenance-matched compiler before removing the merge blocker.
This documentation update passes `git diff --check`, the source-length gate, and plan-section
uniqueness (486 numbered sections); no source parser, compiler build, test, or replay was run.

### 23.27.457 Prove DArray iterator invalidation through local aliases (2026-10-13)

The iterator-invalidation pass now resolves bounded chains of local reference aliases and applies
that resolution to relocating method receivers. This closes a gap where `alias = &xs; alias.push(..)`
inside `for value in xs:` was not connected to the live iterator's source, even though mutable-ref
function arguments already used the alias map. The resolver is a small production module with a
recursive lookup specification, scan invariants, a recursive bounded-resolution model, and a loop
invariant connecting production traversal to that model. Alias initializers, bare identifier copies,
and rebinding assignments are collected across control flow. Duplicate alias names resolve to the
empty sentinel so branch-dependent targets and shadowed scopes remain conservative. Cycles also
return the empty sentinel, and consumers treat it as possibly naming the active source. Ten positive

Scoped callee resolution now returns the selected module path with its source line. Type-bound return
recovery matches both fields, so line directives or separate modules with repeated line numbers cannot
redirect the recovered return type to another same-named function. Static review confirmed the
checker call graph gives executable source functions precedence over same-named externs, while a
separate reachability analysis rejects unsafe callable-extern paths. Diff and source-length gates
pass; no parser/build/runtime run was performed.

### 23.27.544 Specify the complete arena shape dispatch (2026-10-13)

Resource binding, summary, event, call, and structural node shapes now have exact recognized-kind

used only local type stubs for typed-literal decoding and the separate frame-policy validator; the full
proof project remains unqualified against its configured compiler pin.

### 23.27.698 Fail closed on frame imports and scope callee recovery (2026-10-13)

Frame producer preparation now skips frame-event extraction when report annotations contain an

Type-bound call return recovery supplies source annotations to the scoped resolver, which excludes

caller-module precedence is implemented and statically inspected against the checker. Remaining:
frame event generation still invokes some name-and-line owner/policy lookups after resolving a callee,

### 23.27.645 Reuse arena verdicts within one immutable tactic trace (2026-10-13)

Tactic step and branch admission can validate several roots over the same arena. Those private
paths now share one validation workspace, including visited-depth and validity arrays, so a
previously validated subgraph can be reused and the O(nodes) workspace initialization occurs once
per tactic operation. Reuse is explicitly enabled only by the private tactic helpers that retain
the same arena reference across the root checks; general workspace entry points force fresh array
initialization, preserving safety when a caller supplies another same-sized arena. This also lets
the cumulative trace meter charge first-use work and only incremental work for later roots. Static
call-graph review only; no build or runtime qualification was run. Tactic JSON source-annotation
copy is also charged against the cumulative action-AST meter before the copy begins; the existing
action census continues to charge annotation work during tactic execution.

Superseded for frame identity safety by §23.27.545: frame recovery now fails closed when the later
name-and-line owner lookup is ambiguous. The type-bound caller budget was addressed in §23.27.539.

### 23.27.699 Bound scoped resolution by the type-bound caller budget (2026-10-13)

Type-bound replay seeds the shared frame resolver meter at the offset corresponding to the caller's
remaining 1 MiB allowance, then debits the measured resolver work back into the caller counter. This
makes the resolver stop at the caller's ceiling rather than its larger standalone frame ceiling.
Diff and source-length gates pass; no parser/build qualification was run.

### 23.27.545 Close replay identity ambiguity; keep type witnesses about types (2026-10-13)

Frame source-call recovery now validates that the selected name and line still identify exactly one
owner before downstream name-and-line-only policy/event helpers run. This conservatively rejects
same-line declarations in separate modules instead of allowing the later lookup to select or
conflate another owner. Type-bound call-result facts resolve the exact function declaration and use
its declared return type only. They make no claim about purity, totality, or value. Positional and
named arguments are mapped to source formals; labels must be unique and known, positional arguments
must precede named arguments, and every omitted formal must have a default. Type-only lookup may use
a lemma caller's module scope while still excluding lemma callees. Static diff and source-length
checks pass; parser/build/runtime qualification remains pending.

### 23.27.547 Separate type-query caller policy from frame caller policy (2026-10-13)

The shared scoped resolver now exposes an explicit caller-kind policy. Frame source-call recovery
retains its lemma-caller rejection; type-bound return-type lookup may resolve from a lemma's module
scope, while lemma callees remain excluded. This supports type-only facts in lemma bodies without
claiming that those calls are executable or pure. Diff and source-length checks pass; parser/build
qualification remains pending.

### 23.27.548 Reject cross-module nominal and generic return-name collisions (2026-10-13)

Type-bound call-result replay now rejects a return identifier that is a generic binder on the
selected callee declaration, and its legacy file-wide scalar alias lookup refuses any same-spelled

a nominal return type. The aggregate scan is intentionally conservative until the type resolver
uses the selected module path; valid cross-module aliases with colliding names may still be
refused. Source diff and length checks remain the only qualification performed here.

### 23.27.549 Use live lexical scope for frame call shadowing (2026-10-13)

Frame source-call recovery now reuses the replay call-site scope walker. A local callable declared

parameter or local live at the exact call remains a hard rejection. The legacy whole-body binder
scan was removed. Diff and source-length checks pass; parser/build qualification remains pending.

### 23.27.546 Specify bounded postorder arena admission (2026-10-13)

Arena admission now specifies its node and child budgets, the validity of every admitted node
shape, and the child-table range and postorder constraints for every node family that stores a

stubs typed-literal decoding, frame policy shape validation, and the separate semantic child
validator; the full proof project remains unqualified against its configured compiler pin. Diff
and source-length gates pass.

### 23.27.550 Validate replay roots with empty fact sets (2026-10-13)

Arena traversal previously placed the goal on its worklist but drained that list only inside the

Diff and source-length gates pass.

Scoped frame call resolution now checks the caller and callee lemma markers once each, then passes

### 23.27.552 Resolve frame calls inside conditional expressions at the exact site (2026-10-13)

Frame call discovery no longer rejects a call merely because it occurs in a short-circuit

Static diff and source-length checks pass. Runtime qualification remains pending. Local scalar
fact helpers still use a conservative file-wide fallback because their callers do not yet carry

Report-backed frame producer and validator paths now pass `source_annotations` into event

The arena work charge now guarantees that successful charges leave the counter at or below the

### 23.27.555 Resolve call-result aliases in the selected module path (2026-10-13)

Type-bound call-result witnesses now classify the selected callee's declared return type in its

Function and lemma finding summaries now build bounded row chains alongside their existing
name-hash indexes. A finding for an ambiguous declaration name visits only that name's rows,
instead of rescanning every function or lemma for every finding. Index construction, probes, and row
visits share the scheduler's source-work meter, and malformed or inconsistent duplicate chains

the proof binary is not provenance-matched to the current source.

### 23.27.720 Reuse source-bound type module-alias indexes (2026-10-14)

Qualified const-enum and call-result type replay now reuse the complete module-alias index retained
in the private, source-bound fact-call snapshot when its source identity matches the report.
Compatibility reports still build a bounded index from their current annotations, since those
inputs are mutable. This avoids rebuilding annotation tables for each qualified type witness
without trusting cache state for source-unbound reports. The bounded const-enum exclusion
helper was split into its own include so the witness implementation stays below the 600-line source
limit. The plan now distinguishes resolver implementation from the missing true-module-alias fixture
and mutated-mapping refusal control.
Static diff and source-length gates pass; parser/build/replay remain held.

### 23.27.721 Keep opaque extern registration state separate from the alias census (2026-10-14)

The earlier 23.27.713 producer updated the raw alias index while discovering opaque externs. The
producer now leaves the explicit alias census immutable and uses bounded fixed-capacity seen-name
tables for each collection pass. Separate global and synthetic-root sets preserve Stage1's
ambiguous-module-alias behavior, while avoiding a full hash-index rebuild per extern. Source

diff and source-length gates pass. The neighboring compiler worktree is dirty at `2432de75f` and
does not provide matching proof/Stage1 provenance, so this does not establish runtime parity.

### 23.27.722 Preserve replay-gap status in report output (2026-10-14)

Summary and full JSON output previously checked `source_complete` before `replay_complete`, making

### 23.27.723 Replay globally unique aliases for enum witnesses (2026-10-14)

Operator-enum witness resolution now applies Stage1's file-wide unique-alias fallback only after
exact-owner and root lookups miss. The producer checks raw imports in the visible module scope and
uses annotation scope plus imported-name metadata for wildcard, selective, using-member, and

rejects raw AST imports in the fallback path, checks annotation-scoped import shadowing, then performs the

compiler-backed validation remains held until proof and Stage1 source provenance match.

**Superseded detail:** The raw-`Ast::Decl.Import` and annotation-scope shadow checks described
above were removed after tracing Stage1's parser and resolver. Include declarations are expanded
before proof parsing, and enum-owner lookup consumes the file-wide, duplicate-sensitive
`imported_modules` rows without filtering by annotation scope; selective `using Module::Member`
rows live separately and do not participate in that lookup. See 23.27.725 and 23.27.732 for the
current producer/replay rule.

### 23.27.726 Cache owner-ranked enum-name census for operator witnesses (2026-10-14)

Producer and replay const-enum type-path resolvers now use bounded owner-aware enum-name indexes,
then follow only the queried name's collision chain to count exact-scope, root, and file-wide
candidates. The producer reuses its once-built source index; replay independently builds its index
from the replay source in the per-report deterministic replay cache. Alias expansion shares each
index through its recursive type-path walk, replacing repeated full declaration-tree census passes
while preserving owner ranking and fail-closed budget checks. The earlier raw-`Ast::Decl.Import`
fallback guard was removed after checking the Stage1 parser boundary: includes are expanded before

deterministic call replay cache is now opaque: its declaration, alias, cast-site, enum, and

mutable arrays. Enum and import-scan cache state is keyed to report-object and source-file identity
and rebuilt on a mismatch. Index construction and probes use their respective work counters;
malformed array alignment,
exhausted work, or invalid chain termination rejects the witness. Static diff/source-length gates
pass. Parser/build/replay qualification still requires a proof/Stage1 provenance-matched tuple.

### 23.27.728 Index duplicate-module focus finding attribution (2026-10-14)

Focused verification's proposition-finding filter previously scanned every function row for each

### 23.27.724 Specify declaration-identity function focus (2026-10-14)

`--function-json` now accepts a canonical selector such as `Outer::Inner::worker` and resolves its

The focused-function regression now includes direct selection of

### 23.27.726 Exercise cross-module global enum-alias replay fallback (2026-10-14)

The enum alias precedence fixture now contains a consumer module that uses a uniquely named

### 23.27.724 Meter AST-to-kernel source mirror traversal (2026-10-14)

The recursive AST/kernel mirror check now charges every visited source/kernel node pair, the

now asserts the recursive and wrapper-label charges. `git diff --check` and source-length gates
pass; parser/build/replay validation remains held until proof and Stage1 source provenance match.

### 23.27.725 Close bare-alias fallback under wildcard imports (2026-10-14)

This import-shadow behavior was subsumed by the owner-ranked enum/alias resolver in item 23.27.732.

### 23.27.729 Bind replayed quantifier blocks to synthesized binder positions (2026-10-14)

The quantifier parser records the head token's complete `Pos` and byte offset in the

Stage1 qualification.

### 23.27.730 Split semantic diagnostic admission policy (2026-10-14)

The semantic diagnostic classification helpers now live in a dedicated checker include instead
of the public API module. Their behavior is unchanged; the move keeps `check/api.elisa` within its

source-length gate pass; compiler-backed validation remains held until proof and Stage1 source

### 23.27.731 Keep mutable-counter proof summary internal (2026-10-14)

`proof_report_all_obligations_proven` compared only mutable report counters and did not establish

### 23.27.732 Preserve Stage1 imported-module enum resolution order (2026-10-14)

Producer and replay enum witnesses now resolve indexed exact-owner enums, every imported-module

### 23.27.733 Guard pattern-literal producer/replay correspondence (2026-10-14)

Added a pre-build registered source regression for the collision defense. It checks that string and char

### 23.27.734 Guard incremental scheduler finding summaries (2026-10-14)

Added a pre-build source regression for function and lemma scheduling. It requires summary extension

### 23.27.735 Guard source-authorized proof status boundaries (2026-10-14)

Added a pre-build static guard requiring replay receipts, source analyses, and checked views to keep

Trust-boundary review found that `proof_checked_view_report` is still a read-only projection of the

The diagnostic accessor still exposes the raw producer report, so the explicit name improves intent
